facts.label: Evidence that cuts the other way
facts.text: The strongest case against caution is operational momentum: Quarterly Paid Employers rose about a tenth year on year to 73,929 in Q3 2026, revenue grew 8.23% and Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled, while the debt claim has been cut by more than half at a discount. It would win if Adjusted EBITDA holds near the Q3 level of USD 20.8 million a quarter while stock-based compensation stays near USD 7.0 million, which would take reported EBITDA to an annualised USD 55.0 million against the trailing USD 29.1 million; it loses if revenue per employer keeps falling (USD 1,683 against USD 1,717 a year earlier) and the labour market stays subdued. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 28, 30 and 31; calculation C28; calculation C29

facts.label: Company description and credit linkage
facts.text: ZipRecruiter runs a two-sided online marketplace in which employers pay subscription or per-click fees to post and distribute jobs and job seekers use it free. The revenue model is short-cycle: subscription plans run from a day to a year and are recognised ratably, performance-based campaigns last one to three months, and the company reports no material remaining performance obligations, so revenue visibility for debt service is measured in months, not years. Offsetting that, no customer is 10% or more of revenue, revenue outside the United States is under 2%, and 76.88% of FY2025 revenue was subscription, which is non-refundable and cancelable only at the end of its term. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 16 and 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 97, 98 and 123; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K10

facts.text: Revenue follows the number of paying employers and what each spends. Quarterly Paid Employers were 73,929 in Q3 2026 against 66,959 a year earlier, while revenue per paid employer was USD 1,683 against USD 1,717, so growth is volume-led and pricing power is not evident. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is another fall in employer hiring demand, or a loss of search or generative AI traffic, that cuts Quarterly Paid Employers by more than the normal fourth-quarter dip of 11.73%. The first operational break is a fall in paid employers while marketing spend per employer rises, which compresses revenue; with gross margin of 89.25% and a fall-through of 81.64% in FY2025, a repeat of that year's 5.28% revenue fall would remove about USD 19.9 million of trailing reported EBITDA, leaving about USD 9.2 million. Free cash flow would shrink toward the FY2025 trough, but at the lower coupon that trough would be about USD 19.2 million rather than USD 3.5 million, so cash of USD 174.7 million would not be at risk from debt service; the real exposure is the combination of that earnings fall with buybacks drawing on the USD 107.3 million of authorisation and a refinancing in 2030 that needs a market window. Management levers are marketing cuts, headcount, stopping buybacks and further discounted note purchases. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, ZipRecruiter presents an adequate but fragile business profile supported by a debt claim cut by more than half, cash of USD 174.7 million and light capital needs, but credit quality is constrained by thin and cyclical earnings, founder control and a record of large buybacks. Cash-flow durability appears adequate rather than strong because free cash flow of USD 27.4 million over the last twelve months came after a year of only USD 3.5 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on free cash flow of about USD 23.07 million a year to 2030 and on market access that the notes' 83.49% fair value ratio does not yet confirm. The primary downside path is another hiring downturn with high fall-through to EBITDA while buybacks continue. Further analysis would require the indenture, the proxy statement, management guidance and market quotes. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: a hiring downturn that cuts earnings while cash is still being distributed to shareholders. ### Bottom line

spans.text: ## Request

Financial foundation for Ziprecruiter, Inc. (zip-1617553), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit_snapshot pathway (full credit assessment). The scope is the consolidated income statement, cash flow statement, balance sheet, debt, liquidity and leverage metrics built from the five supplied SEC filings, with Q3 2026 as the current period and FY2025 as the prior period.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_zip-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of Ziprecruiter, Inc. for the year ended 31 December 2024 | 2025-02-25 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 4c6af145b03114d7fc912e17b781557c30eaf55222c72a7a1e2ec997aad65c29 | FY2023 balance sheet and Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation; FY2024 revolving facility availability |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of Ziprecruiter, Inc. for the year ended 31 December 2025 | 2026-02-25 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 6dfe6d458eadd70f776719e563c19476bcf176d4563b526b71feb00c5d33eb46 | Audited FY2023 to FY2025 income statement and cash flow, FY2024 and FY2025 balance sheets, debt note, Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, commitments and leases |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_zip-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Ziprecruiter, Inc. for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 | 2026-05-07 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 5e50a7cc70946277b7a20b88ef836cbbcfa0d0dd3d289ffc085bf555703efc7f | Quarterly figures and the facility expiry subsequent event |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_zip-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Ziprecruiter, Inc. for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 | 2026-08-05 (signature date; filing date not stated) | b52e8b008cdcfe329007adb1e5461c18705547e8db0ac74d8a5ed84b46d67915 | Second quarter 2026 figures, June 2026 note repurchase, balance sheet at 2026-06-30 |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Ziprecruiter, Inc. for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 | 2026-11-09 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 02a71bc8b05fc313332809859cd2714710e240d686bc1d6349f7b0b2e3bd1a83 | Current period statements, debt, liquidity, nine-month 2025 comparatives, Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation and subsequent items |
Supplied handoffs:
| Module | Handoff | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | CP-0 source readiness for Ziprecruiter, Inc. | 4e707b7bff84f222add8c3e3e640800cbda009dd7deba9c6b7f2174000e0b825 | Source gate, gaps on the indenture, guarantors and ratings, and the period coverage statement |
## Findings
### Bottom line

ZipRecruiter's creditors hold a claim less than half its former size after the 2026 note buyback, with USD 248.7 million of debt against USD 174.7 million of cash, but earnings remain thin: trailing debt is 8.53x reported EBITDA.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C7

On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, which adds back stock-based compensation, trailing leverage is 4.06x and net leverage 1.21x; on reported EBITDA net leverage is 2.54x, and FY2025 reported EBITDA was negative. No revolver remains and cash interest paid for the trailing year is not disclosed, so trailing interest cover is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21 and 30; calculation C6; calculation C9; calculation C10
### Leverage trajectory and drivers

Total debt at carrying value fell from USD 544.8 million at FY2025 to USD 248.7 million at 2026-09-30 because the company bought back USD 299.3 million of principal of its 2030 notes at about 79 cents on the dollar, so what remains for creditors is the USD 250.7 million of notes. The cash used came from the balance sheet, not from earnings: cash and marketable securities together fell from USD 409.1 million to USD 174.7 million, a fall of USD 234.4 million, and the USD 60.0 million gain on the buyback (the discount to par net of fees and the write-off of issuance costs) accounts for almost all of the fall in net debt after marketable securities from USD 135.6 million to USD 74.0 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 7 and 21; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C30

Before the buyback the problem was earnings, not debt. Debt at carrying value stayed between USD 542.6 million and USD 544.8 million from FY2023 to FY2025 while Adjusted EBITDA fell from USD 175.3 million to USD 40.8 million and reported EBITDA fell from USD 91.1 million to a loss of USD 6.9 million, driven by revenue declines of 26.6% in FY2024 and 5.3% in FY2025. FY2025 leverage was therefore 13.37x on Adjusted EBITDA and could not be calculated on reported EBITDA, and the creditor's cushion rested on cash and marketable securities of USD 409.1 million rather than on earnings.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 72 and 98; calculation C5; calculation C9; calculation C19

The turn in 2026 is visible but young. Nine-month revenue rose 3.79% and Q3 revenue 8.23%, operating income swung by USD 36.8 million to a profit of USD 13.5 million, and Adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.70% in Q3 against 8.04% a year earlier. Most of the swing came from lower costs, not faster growth: operating expenses fell USD 25.151 million against a USD 11.662 million rise in gross profit, with research and development expense down 19.15% and stock-based compensation down 40.56% for the nine months, which also shrinks the add-back that separates adjusted from reported EBITDA.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 30, 36 and 37; calculation C27; calculation C28
### Coverage and cash interest

Interest cover cannot be established for the trailing twelve months because the quarterly reports print no cash interest paid, and interest expense, which is an accrual that includes issuance cost amortisation, is not substituted. The annual figures show reported EBITDA covering cash interest 3.24x in FY2023, 0.48x in FY2024 and not at all in FY2025 (negative 0.24x), while Adjusted EBITDA covered it 6.23x, 2.77x and 1.44x. After the buyback the contractual coupon is USD 12.535 million a year against USD 27.500 million before, which Adjusted EBITDA of USD 61.3 million covers 4.89x and reported EBITDA of USD 29.1 million covers 2.33x; this is a coupon calculation, not cash interest paid.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C21
### Cash flow quality

Free cash flow was USD 92.5 million in FY2023, USD 36.2 million in FY2024, USD 3.5 million in FY2025 and USD 27.4 million for the last twelve months, after capital spending that fell from USD 10.7 million in FY2023 to about USD 7.5 million in FY2025 and the last twelve months, mostly capitalised software. In FY2025 the company spent USD 102.1 million on share repurchases against free cash flow of USD 3.5 million, so distributions to shareholders were funded from the investment portfolio; in the nine months to 2026-09-30 share repurchases of USD 14.0 million were below free cash flow of USD 21.2 million, but USD 107.3 million of authorisation remains and the indenture's limits on restricted payments are not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100 and 101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 24 and 96; calculation C18

Operating cash flow of USD 27.3 million for nine months 2026 includes a non-cash deferred tax add-back of USD 20.3 million, which the issuer attributes to using carried-forward tax losses against the taxable gain on the buyback, so most of the USD 20.2 million income tax expense for the period is not a cash cost; it is also reduced by a USD 10.2 million fall in accrued interest as old coupons were settled. Deferred tax assets fell by USD 20.380 million to USD 54.812 million, so part of the shield against cash taxes has been used; nine-month cash taxes are not printed, and FY2025 cash taxes paid were USD 4.061 million.
### Liquidity adequacy and claims outside debt

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is cash only: USD 174.7 million of cash and equivalents, no marketable securities and no committed facility, because the USD 290.0 million revolver expired unrenewed on 2026-04-30. That cash is 70.25% of carrying debt, so the USD 250.7 million bullet due 2030-01-15, three years and three and a half months away, will need free cash flow or a refinancing for the remainder. Letters of credit are cash collateralised by a restricted deposit of USD 2.1 million that is excluded from cash.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 17 and 21; calculation C4

Claims outside debt are small but real: operating lease liabilities of USD 11.058 million sit outside Total Debt, hosting service purchase commitments were USD 76.5 million in total at FY2025 (USD 15.2 million due in 2026 and USD 16.0 million in each of 2027 to 2029), and a stockholder class action filed on 2026-06-17 over the buyback programme carries no estimate of loss. No pension, factoring, supply chain finance or consent decree funding is disclosed, the company states it has no finance leases, and deferred revenue of USD 11.610 million is too small to be a funding float.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6 and 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 114 and 130; calculation C23; calculation C24
### Evidence that cuts the other way

The strongest case against caution is operational momentum: Quarterly Paid Employers rose about a tenth year on year to 73,929 in Q3 2026, revenue grew 8.23% and Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled, while the debt claim has been cut by more than half at a discount. It would win if Adjusted EBITDA holds near the Q3 level of USD 20.8 million a quarter while stock-based compensation stays near USD 7.0 million, which would take reported EBITDA to an annualised USD 55.0 million against the trailing USD 29.1 million; it loses if revenue per employer keeps falling (USD 1,683 against USD 1,717 a year earlier) and the labour market stays subdued.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 28, 30 and 31; calculation C28; calculation C29
### Subsequent events, multi-figure events and data quality

The credit facility expiry on 2026-04-30 was reported as a subsequent event in the first quarter report and is already in the 2026-09-30 balances; the only dated items after 2026-09-30 are an expected USD 5.7 million tax benefit in Q4 2026 and the 2026-10-28 termination of two executive share-sale plans, none of which changes net debt or is blended into any period figure. The note buyback is one event with several figures: principal USD 299.3 million, price USD 236.8 million including fees, discounted par of USD 233.3 million before fees, cash paid of USD 236.764 million for nine months but only USD 229.684 million for six months, and a gain of USD 60.003 million, which reconcile except for about USD 3.1 million of the June price that the six-month cash flow does not yet show, which the filings do not explain.

spans.text: ## Request

Business and governance fact pack for Ziprecruiter, Inc. (zip-1617553), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit_snapshot pathway (full credit assessment). The scope is the business model, operating model, ownership and control, governance, capital allocation, transaction and event history taken from the five supplied SEC filings; no sponsor material, lender presentation or executed legal document was supplied.
## Sources

Supplied handoffs:
| Module | Handoff | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | CP-0 source readiness for Ziprecruiter, Inc. | 4e707b7bff84f222add8c3e3e640800cbda009dd7deba9c6b7f2174000e0b825 | Source gate, the missing indenture, proxy statement and guarantor information, and the period coverage statement |
## Findings
### Bottom line

ZipRecruiter is a short-cycle, founder-controlled online hiring marketplace whose revenue fell by nearly a third between 2023 and 2025 and is only now recovering, so noteholders depend on management restraint over buybacks that nothing visible in these filings constrains.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 98; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 16, 29 and 90; calculation A2

No sponsor owns it: the chief executive officer holds 78.9% of the votes with 15.7% of the shares, and sponsor and governance risk is Medium. Management retired USD 299.3 million of the notes at a discount in 2026 and has never paid a dividend, but it spent USD 102.1 million on share repurchases in FY2025 while free cash flow was USD 3.5 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21 and 90; 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 84, 100 and 101; calculation A3; calculation A4
### Key findings

- The business is short-cycle and cost-flexible, which gives creditors little revenue visibility but a lever to protect cash. Subscription plans run from a day to a year, performance-based campaigns run for one to three months, the company reports no material remaining performance obligations, and sales and marketing absorbs about half of revenue, most of it advertising that management says it can scale back quickly.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 16, 17, 31 and 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation A5

- Demand fell sharply and is only now turning. Revenue declined 26.59% in FY2024 and 5.28% in FY2025, and in Q3 2026 revenue rose 8.23% and Quarterly Paid Employers 10.41%, but revenue per paid employer fell 1.98%, so the recovery rests on employer count rather than spend per employer.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7 and 28; calculation A2; calculation A6

- Control sits with the founder, not a sponsor, and the board's independence cannot be tested. The chief executive officer is the sole Class B holder with 78.9% of the votes and 15.7% of the shares, the board is classified with staggered terms, and director and officer detail sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 90 and 93; 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 59 and 147; calculation A3

- Capital allocation favoured shareholders until 2026. Share repurchases were USD 147.6 million in FY2023, USD 40.3 million in FY2024 and USD 102.1 million in FY2025, with USD 642.7 million of the USD 750.0 million authorisation used by 2026-09-30, while free cash flow in FY2025 was only USD 3.5 million.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 84, 100 and 101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24 and 96; calculation A4; calculation A8

- The 2026 note repurchase shows willingness to use cash for creditors when debt trades at a discount. USD 299.3 million of principal, 54.4% of the original USD 550.0 million, was retired for USD 236.8 million, and share repurchases fell to USD 14.0 million for nine months, yet the revolving facility was left to lapse, so no committed liquidity backstop remains.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 21 and 24; calculation A8; calculation A9

- No dividend, distribution recapitalisation, creditor exchange or priming has been disclosed, so the supported conduct is mixed rather than adverse, and the sponsor and governance risk level is Medium on limited evidence.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is conduct since mid-2026: management retired more than half of the notes below par, share repurchases dropped below free cash flow, no dividend has ever been paid and no creditor-adverse transaction is disclosed. That evidence would win if the indenture proves to restrict share repurchases tightly enough to make the FY2025 level impossible to repeat, or if free cash flow stays near the USD 27.4 million trailing level while repurchases stay near USD 14.0 million a nine-month period.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 21 and 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; calculation A8

The view would worsen if repurchases resume at the FY2025 pace while earnings are thin, if the remaining USD 107.3 million of authorisation is drawn quickly, or if the chief executive officer's voting control is used to approve a distribution or a transaction that changes the notes' protection; the repurchase programme is already the subject of a stockholder suit filed on 2026-06-17.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 24 and 96
### Limitations
- The indenture is not supplied, so restricted payment capacity is not established and the conclusion that noteholders depend on management restraint cannot be tested against actual covenant limits.

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, director and officer ownership and related-party transactions are not established, and the Medium governance level could move either way once they are known.

- The relationship of the Institutional Venture Partners affiliated holders that sold shares back to the company in FY2025 is not described, so that private repurchase is not classified as related-party conduct.

- No investor presentation or earnings release is supplied, so management's own description of the recovery and of buyback intentions is limited to the filings' wording, which lowers confidence in the demand turn.

- Nothing dated after the quarterly report signed on 2026-11-09 is covered, so a buyback or note transaction in the last weeks before the as-of date would not appear and the 2026 pattern of restraint could already have changed.

The scope is the issuer's overall fundamental credit profile, built from the five supplied SEC filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance outputs; it gives no security recommendation, recovery conclusion or covenant conclusion.

## Findings
### Bottom line

ZipRecruiter's credit is adequate but fragile: USD 174.7 million of cash backs the remaining USD 250.7 million of 2030 notes, but earnings are thin and cyclical and buybacks compete for that cash, so creditors rely on cash and cost cuts, not earnings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6 and 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K1

Trailing reported EBITDA is USD 29.1 million against USD 61.3 million on the issuer's adjusted measure, so leverage is 8.53x or 4.06x, and the run-rate coupon of about USD 12.5 million is covered 2.33x or 4.89x. The primary downside is another hiring downturn, because in FY2025 about 81.64% of lost revenue fell through to reported EBITDA.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K3; calculation K7
### Key findings

- Earnings are thin and lean on an equity-pay add-back, which makes them the weakest part of the credit. Trailing reported EBITDA is USD 29.1 million against USD 61.3 million adjusted, and USD 32.1 million of that gap is stock-based compensation, so leverage is 8.53x on reported and 4.06x on adjusted earnings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation K10

- Liquidity is adequate for the remaining debt but has no committed backstop. Cash of USD 174.7 million covers 69.69% of the USD 250.7 million principal, the revolving facility lapsed on 2026-04-30, and the USD 107.3 million of buyback authorisation left equals 61.41% of that cash.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 21 and 96; calculation K1; calculation K9

- Debt service looks comfortable on the contractual coupon but is unproven on cash paid. The run-rate coupon of about USD 12.5 million is covered 2.33x by reported and 4.89x by adjusted trailing EBITDA, while cash interest paid for the trailing year is not disclosed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K3

- Revenue is cyclical with short visibility, and the 2026 turn is young. Revenue fell 26.59% in FY2024 and 5.28% in FY2025 before rising 8.23% in Q3 2026 on 10.41% more paid employers, and plans run from a day to a year with no material remaining performance obligations.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 17 and 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 98; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K10

- Operating leverage is the main way a downturn reaches creditors. In FY2025 about 81.64% of lost revenue fell through to reported EBITDA because gross margin is 89.25% and only marketing spend flexes quickly.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 98 and 99; calculation K7

- Financial policy has leaned toward shareholders, which keeps governance risk at Medium. A founder holds 78.9% of the votes and FY2025 buybacks of USD 102.1 million dwarfed free cash flow of USD 3.5 million, yet the 2026 repurchase retired USD 299.3 million of notes at a discount.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21 and 90; calculation K10

- Refinancing the 2030 bullet needs free cash flow, not only cash. The USD 76.0 million between principal and cash needs about USD 23.07 million of free cash flow a year to maturity against USD 27.4 million over the last twelve months, ignoring distributions, and the company's own fair value estimate puts the notes at 83.49% of principal.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19 and 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K2; calculation K6
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is the 2026 trend: trailing free cash flow of USD 27.4 million after interest, a coupon cut by more than half, Quarterly Paid Employers up 10.41%, and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 16.70% in Q3 against 8.04% a year earlier. The view would improve if adjusted EBITDA holds near the Q3 level of USD 20.8 million a quarter while stock-based compensation stays near USD 7.0 million, which annualises to USD 55.0 million of reported-equivalent EBITDA, and if buybacks stay near the 2026 pace of USD 14.0 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 28 and 30; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K10; calculation K13

The view would worsen if revenue falls again at the FY2025 pace, which at the observed 81.64% fall-through would cut trailing reported EBITDA by about USD 19.9 million to about USD 9.2 million, if buybacks return to the FY2025 level, or if cash falls toward half the principal while no refinancing is in place.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K7; calculation K8
### Limitations

- No quantitative management guidance or forecast is supplied, so the view of 2027 earnings rests on the 2026 run rate, and a reversal of the hiring recovery would lower the assessment of debt service capacity.

- Covenant levels, call and make-whole terms and the amount of debt the indenture permits are not established, so refinancing capacity is judged on cash and cash flow alone and could be stronger or weaker with those terms.
- The 2026 statements are unaudited and the trailing figures are constructed from them, so the leverage conclusions could move after the FY2026 audit.
- Cash interest paid for the trailing year is not disclosed, so the debt service view uses the contractual coupon, which would be understated if other cash interest items exist.
- No rating or market quote is supplied; the notes' fair value is the company's own estimate in less active markets, so the market-access judgement is indicative only.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The strongest credit support is the smaller debt claim and the cash behind it. The 2026 repurchase retired USD 299.3 million of principal at about 79 cents on the dollar, cutting the run-rate coupon from USD 27.5 million to about USD 12.5 million a year and leaving USD 174.7 million of cash against USD 250.7 million of principal, so a refinancing gap of USD 76.0 million remains over roughly three and a quarter years.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6 and 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K1; calculation K3; calculation K6

A second support is a business that converts to cash when costs are managed: free cash flow was USD 27.4 million over the last twelve months after interest, capital spending is light at about USD 7.5 million a year, and marketing and advertising of about 29.79% of revenue can be cut quickly. That matters because it gives management a lever to protect cash before debt service is touched.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7 and 14; calculation K10

A third support is the audited, regular reporting and the absence of any disclosed creditor-adverse transaction, exchange or priming, together with no dividend ever paid, which keeps monitoring straightforward and the conduct record clean to date.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95

The main weakness is thin, cyclical earnings. Reported EBITDA was a loss of USD 6.9 million in FY2025 and is USD 29.1 million on a trailing basis, and the issuer's adjusted measure adds back USD 32.1 million of stock-based compensation, which is 52.42% of adjusted EBITDA, so lenders cannot treat the adjusted figure as cash earnings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K10; calculation K12

A second weakness is revenue that follows hiring demand with little contractual cover: revenue fell 26.59% in FY2024 and 5.28% in FY2025, and the observed fall-through of 81.64% in FY2025 shows how fast lost revenue reaches EBITDA, so a downturn would erode cash quickly.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 98 and 99; calculation K7

A third weakness is that liquidity is cash only: the revolving facility lapsed on 2026-04-30, and a buyback authorisation of USD 107.3 million remains against USD 174.7 million of cash, so the same cash backs both distributions and the 2030 bullet.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21 and 96; calculation K9

A fourth weakness is founder control and the FY2025 buyback of USD 102.1 million against free cash flow of USD 3.5 million, with the indenture's limits on distributions not visible, so protection against a repeat depends on management restraint.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 90

### Company description and credit linkage

ZipRecruiter runs a two-sided online marketplace in which employers pay subscription or per-click fees to post and distribute jobs and job seekers use it free. The revenue model is short-cycle: subscription plans run from a day to a year and are recognised ratably, performance-based campaigns last one to three months, and the company reports no material remaining performance obligations, so revenue visibility for debt service is measured in months, not years. Offsetting that, no customer is 10% or more of revenue, revenue outside the United States is under 2%, and 76.88% of FY2025 revenue was subscription, which is non-refundable and cancelable only at the end of its term.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 16 and 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 97, 98 and 123; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K10
### Ownership and group structure

The company is founder-led and listed, with no sponsor or parent: the chief executive officer holds 78.9% of the votes with 15.7% of the shares through Class B stock, the board is classified, and the notes are the obligation of the listed company, with guarantees mentioned but no guarantor named. Creditors therefore have no sponsor to support or extract value, and the financial policy that matters is the board's under one holder's control; structural priority and guarantor coverage cannot be assessed until the indenture is supplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 90 and 93; 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 128
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue follows the number of paying employers and what each spends. Quarterly Paid Employers were 73,929 in Q3 2026 against 66,959 a year earlier, while revenue per paid employer was USD 1,683 against USD 1,717, so growth is volume-led and pricing power is not evident. Demand is cyclical and discretionary: employers cut hiring budgets in 2023 to 2025, and traffic depends in part on search and generative AI engines and Job Distribution Partners that the company does not control, so a change in those channels could raise acquisition cost.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 53 and 58; 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 73–75; calculation K10
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Gross margin is 89.25%, so almost all lost revenue reaches operating profit unless costs are cut, which is why the fall-through in FY2025 was 81.64%. Costs flex in two layers: marketing and advertising of USD 104.3 million for nine months 2026 can be scaled quickly, while research and development and general expenses moved only with headcount, and research and development fell 19.15% for nine months 2026 as staff were cut. Stock-based compensation fell 40.56% to USD 22.8 million for nine months, which shrinks the gap between adjusted and reported EBITDA but not the cash cost of tax withholding on equity awards.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 98, 99 and 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 10, 14 and 37; calculation K7; calculation K10
### Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion

Capital needs are light: purchases of property and capitalised software were about USD 7.5 million in FY2025, and the business has no maintenance and growth split, no pension or finance lease debt and only USD 11.1 million of operating lease liabilities. Free cash flow was USD 3.5 million in FY2025 and USD 27.4 million over the last twelve months, so conversion of adjusted EBITDA to free cash flow was 44.78% on the trailing figures; the main leaks are buybacks, tax withholding on equity awards and, once the loss carry-forwards used against the 2026 gain are gone, cash taxes.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6 and 42; calculation K10; calculation K14
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense in a fragmented market that includes larger platforms such as Indeed, LinkedIn and Google, which limits pricing power and keeps marketing intensity high. Entry and substitution risk comes from generative AI and direct employer channels, buyer power is moderate because employers can switch freely but none is 10% or more of revenue, and supplier power sits with search engines, Job Distribution Partners and the cloud host, for which USD 76.5 million of hosting commitments run through 2030 and beyond.
### Macro, regulatory and technology factors

The labour market is the dominant macro driver: the company calls it subdued and ties revenue to hiring demand, with the fourth quarter seasonally weaker. Privacy, data protection and artificial intelligence rules apply in the United States, Canada, the European Union, the United Kingdom and Israel and could raise costs, and generative AI changes how job seekers find jobs, which bears on traffic; neither factor is quantified in the filings, so both stay watch items rather than drivers.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 13 and 75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31 and 53
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are a smaller debt claim, cash of USD 174.7 million, light capital needs and flexible marketing spend; weaknesses are thin reported earnings, short revenue visibility, no committed facility and founder control with a history of large buybacks. The only opportunities that would lift credit quality are a sustained recovery in employer count and spend and the repurchase of more notes below par; the threats are another hiring downturn, a loss of search or AI traffic and a return of large distributions.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6 and 28
### Financial profile and credit quality

On the nine financial profile dimensions the assessments are: scale and market position Average, because trailing revenue of USD 461.7 million is meaningful but the company faces larger platforms; competitive advantage Average, because matching technology and brand exist but switching costs are low; business diversification Weak, because revenue comes from one marketplace for one customer type; cost and capex flexibility Average to Strong, because marketing is variable and capital needs are light; margin stability Weak, because reported EBITDA swung from USD 91.1 million to a loss within two years; free cash flow stability Weak to Average, because free cash flow ranged from USD 92.5 million to USD 3.5 million; ability to refinance Average, with cash covering 69.69% of principal but no market quote and the notes at 83.49% of principal by the company's own estimate; liquidity position Average, because cash is substantial but there is no committed facility; and financial policy and governance Weak to Average, given founder control and past buybacks balanced by the 2026 deleveraging.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19 and 28; calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K10

The trend is improving from a low point: trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 61.3 million compares with USD 40.8 million for FY2025, and debt is less than half its former level, but the improvement is one year old and rests partly on cost cuts and lower equity pay.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K10
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the supports are rising paid employer counts, the halved coupon and a cost base cut by headcount reductions; the headwinds are a labour market the company still calls subdued, seasonally weaker fourth quarters, falling revenue per employer and the unknown pace of buybacks. Over three to five years the 2030 maturity dominates: the company must bridge USD 76.0 million between cash and principal from free cash flow or a refinancing, and the call price falls to par on 2027-01-15, which makes a later refinancing cheaper to execute.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 28 and 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 75 and 129; calculation K6
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is another fall in employer hiring demand, or a loss of search or generative AI traffic, that cuts Quarterly Paid Employers by more than the normal fourth-quarter dip of 11.73%. The first operational break is a fall in paid employers while marketing spend per employer rises, which compresses revenue; with gross margin of 89.25% and a fall-through of 81.64% in FY2025, a repeat of that year's 5.28% revenue fall would remove about USD 19.9 million of trailing reported EBITDA, leaving about USD 9.2 million. Free cash flow would shrink toward the FY2025 trough, but at the lower coupon that trough would be about USD 19.2 million rather than USD 3.5 million, so cash of USD 174.7 million would not be at risk from debt service; the real exposure is the combination of that earnings fall with buybacks drawing on the USD 107.3 million of authorisation and a refinancing in 2030 that needs a market window. Management levers are marketing cuts, headcount, stopping buybacks and further discounted note purchases. The observable triggers are paid employers, adjusted EBITDA margin back below 8.04%, cash below half the principal and any return of FY2025-scale buybacks.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 28 and 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_zip-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 98; calculation K4; calculation K7; calculation K8; calculation K9; calculation K11
### Overall credit view

Overall, ZipRecruiter presents an adequate but fragile business profile supported by a debt claim cut by more than half, cash of USD 174.7 million and light capital needs, but credit quality is constrained by thin and cyclical earnings, founder control and a record of large buybacks. Cash-flow durability appears adequate rather than strong because free cash flow of USD 27.4 million over the last twelve months came after a year of only USD 3.5 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on free cash flow of about USD 23.07 million a year to 2030 and on market access that the notes' 83.49% fair value ratio does not yet confirm. The primary downside path is another hiring downturn with high fall-through to EBITDA while buybacks continue. Further analysis would require the indenture, the proxy statement, management guidance and market quotes. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: a hiring downturn that cuts earnings while cash is still being distributed to shareholders.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_zip-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 19 and 21; calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K6; calculation K10
